circle.definition: Ellipse in which the two axes are of equal length.

square.definition: (geometry) a plane rectangle with four equal sides and four right angles.

triangle.definition: Something approximating the shape of a triangle.

rectangle.definition: A parallelogram with four right angles.

oval.definition: A closed plane curve resulting from the intersection of a circular cone and a plane cutting completely through it.

diamond.definition: A transparent piece of diamond that has been cut and polished and is valued as a precious gem.

pentagon.definition: A government building with five sides that serves as the headquarters of the United States Department of Defense.

hexagon.definition: A flat shape with six straight sides.

octagon.definition: A flat shape with eight straight sides.

star.definition: Indicating the most important performer or role.

sphere.definition: A particular environment or walk of life.

cube.definition: A three-dimensional shape with six square or rectangular sides.

cylinder.definition: A surface generated by rotating a parallel line around a fixed line.

cone.definition: A shape whose base is a circle and whose sides taper up to a point.

pyramid.definition: A massive monument with a square base and four triangular sides.

prism.definition: A polyhedron with two congruent and parallel faces (the bases) and whose lateral faces are parallelograms.

cuboid.definition: A solid shape with six rectangular faces.

hemisphere.definition: Half of a sphere or globe.

torus.definition: A ring-shaped surface generated by rotating a circle around an axis that does not intersect the circle.

tetrahedron.definition: Any polyhedron having four plane faces.

line.definition: A formation of people or things one beside another.

curve.definition: A line on a graph representing data.

zigzag.definition: In a zigzag course or on a zigzag path.

spiral.definition: A curve that lies on the surface of a cylinder or cone and cuts the element at a constant angle.

right-angle.definition: An angle measuring exactly 90 degrees is formed when two lines, rays, or segments meet perpendicularly.

acute-angle.definition: An angle measuring more than zero degrees and less than ninety degrees, narrower than a right angle.

obtuse-angle.definition: An angle is obtuse when it measures more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees.

parallel.definition: An imaginary line around the Earth parallel to the equator.

perpendicular.definition: At right angles to the plane of the horizon or a base line.

area.definition: The extent of a 2-dimensional surface enclosed within a boundary.

perimeter.definition: The boundary line or the area immediately inside the boundary.

volume.definition: The amount of 3-dimensional space occupied by an object.

radius.definition: A straight line from the center to the perimeter of a circle (or from the center to the surface of a sphere).

diameter.definition: A straight line connecting the center of a circle with two points on its perimeter (or the center of a sphere with two points on its surface).

circumference.definition: The boundary line encompassing an area or object.

diagonal.definition: (mathematics) a set of entries in a square matrix running diagonally either from the upper left to lower right entry or running from the upper right to lower left entry.

symmetry.definition: (mathematics) an attribute of a shape or relation.

edge.definition: A line determining the limits of an area.

repeat.definition: To do, say, or show something again.

sequence.definition: Serial arrangement in which things follow in logical order or a recurrent pattern.

pattern.definition: A repeated arrangement of shapes, colors, or objects.

tessellation.definition: The careful juxtaposition of shapes in a pattern.

fractal.definition: (mathematics) a geometric pattern that is repeated at every scale and so cannot be represented by classical geometry.

grid.definition: A pattern of regularly spaced horizontal and vertical lines.

array.definition: An ordered arrangement of objects, often in rows and columns.

matrix.definition: (mathematics) a rectangular array of quantities or expressions set out by rows and columns.

kaleidoscope.definition: A complex pattern of constantly changing colors and shapes.
